function: Downlink CSI feedback: UT encoder compresses CSI (ratio 1/8), BS decoder reconstructs it; meta-transfer learning adapts the model to new environments (p. 2, p. 4).
system: FDD massive MIMO OFDM; BS with 32 transmit antennas and UT with 2 (per Table II); 2.0 GHz uplink, 2.1 GHz downlink, 50 MHz (p. 2, p. 4).
method: Conv encoder and residual-block decoder (CSI autoencoder); MSE pre-training, meta-learning (MAML) with scale-and-shift, online fine-tuning, federated fine-tuning option (p. 2, p. 3).
data_channel: Simulated 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL-A to CDL-E channels: CDL-A 50000 samples, CDL-B/C 4000 each, CDL-D 4000, CDL-E 2000 (1000 adaptation, 1000 validation) (p. 4).
test_conditions: Offline pre- and meta-training, then online adaptation to a new environment with 100-1000 samples (CDL-E adaptation set), evaluated on 1000 validation samples (p. 2, p. 4, p. 5).
baselines: Learned: transfer learning [11], meta-learning (MAML) [12]; variants: freezing scheme, without S&S, simplified scheme; centralized learning versus FL; no non-learned baseline (p. 4).
metrics: NMSE (dB) versus fine-tuning epochs, number of fine-tuning samples and number of users; number of fine-tuned parameters, convergence time, FLOPs (p. 4, p. 5).
complexity: FLOPs 0.775M (meta-learning 0.902M); fine-tuned parameters 15400 versus 50186 for transfer learning; convergence time 850 s versus 1750 s (p. 4, p. 5).
q1_support: p. 4: "The NR CDL channel model defined by TR38.901"; the CDL-A to CDL-E datasets are generated from the 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL profiles with the parameters of Table II.
q2_support: p. 4: "into an adaptation set and a validation set"; p. 2: "we fine-tune the model with a small number of samples to" adapt; the model is adapted to a new CDL environment (CDL-E) with 100 to 1000 samples (Fig. 5) and evaluated on held-out validation samples.
q3_support: p. 4: "Here, transfer learning and meta-learning as two baseline"; p. 1: "traditional methods, such as compressive sensing and static" codebooks appear only in the introduction; the schemes in Fig. 4 are all learned or variants of the proposed scheme, so no non-learned baseline is compared.
q4_support: p. 5: "proposed scheme is 0.775M, which is less than that of the" meta-learning scheme (0.902M FLOPs); Table IV (p. 4) gives 15400 fine-tuning parameters versus 50186 for transfer learning and convergence time 850 s versus 1750 s.
q5_support: p. 4: "The structure of the generated data sample is of"; the samples are generated by the authors from the CDL profiles (Table II), and no code or data link, DOI or release statement appears in the paper.
notes: PDF checked: title and DOI 10.1109/LWC.2024.3511553 on p. 1 match. Included, area 2 (CSI feedback); federated learning only fine-tunes the model online with digital gradient aggregation (p. 3), so not area 7. Tables II to IV and Figs. 4 to 6 were read from the page images, since they are missing from the extracted text. The text gives [32 x 14 x 2 x 72] as subcarriers x symbols x receive x transmit antennas, but Table II lists 72 subcarriers and 32 transmit antennas. The paper does not say which CDL sets are used for pre-training and meta-training; CDL-E is the set split into adaptation and validation sets. q3 is 0 because every compared scheme is learned or a variant of the proposed one.
